deadline.value: Deadlines are set by each funded project or funding competition. The department's fully funded October 2027 studentships close 8 Jan 2027 but are for home-fee students only, so international applicants usually aim for the President's PhD Scholarship rounds: 2 Nov 2026, 11 Jan 2027 or 1 Mar 2027 (23:59 UK time).
deadline.quote: Applicants who apply by 23:59 (UK time) 2 November 2026 and are awarded a scholarship will be notified by 31 January 2027. | Applicants who apply by 23:59 (UK time) 11 January 2027 | Applicants who apply by 23:59 (UK time) 1 March 2027

also.quote: The deadline for applying for admission is generally set by the programme or the funding competition for which you are applying.

supervisor.value: Unless you apply to a specific funded project or programme, you must identify and contact a prospective supervisor in Life Sciences before you submit an application.
supervisor.quote: If you are not applying for a specific programme then you should in the first instance identify and make contact with an academic member of staff as a prospective supervisor prior to submitting an application.

funding.value: The department's fully funded studentships (UK fees plus a UKRI stipend of GBP 23,805) are for home-fee students only. International applicants need the competitive President's PhD Scholarship, another college-wide or external scholarship, or self-funding.
funding.quote: Unfortunately, international students are not eligible for this call.

also.quote: This competitive scheme has higher than usual eligibility requirements, attracting candidates that show excellent academic performance and promising research potential.

entry_route.value: You need a bachelor's at UK first-class or 2:1 standard (or the overseas equivalent); some projects also require a master's, and studentship adverts may prefer applicants with one.
entry_route.quote: Have or expect to have a BSc degree of 1st class or 2.1 standard in UK system, or equivalent for overseas degrees. A Masters degree may also be required.

also.quote: Candidates with a master’s degree in addition to a BSc may be given preference.

notes: Projects span Life Science disciplines 'from molecular structures to global ecology'. The department often asks for higher grades than the College minimum for overseas degrees, so check each studentship advert.
